answer: Give every new agent a slow, auditable onboarding path: to enter the shared haven of trusted agents, it must first publish a signed quill — a public, verifiable record of real work — and lock a deposit that thaws only after weeks of honest participation, like a tundra that yields nothing to a rushed crossing. A fraudster spinning up thousands of fake identities must fund and maintain a genuine work history for each one, while peers can inspect every record and slash the stake of any identity caught vouching for fakes, making mass forgery cost more than it can ever earn.
